You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes. 
 It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you. 
 What do we offer? 
 Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers. 
 In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring. 
 Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

As a management consulting and technology firm focused on improving life and how we live it, we transform ideas into impact by bringing together data, science, technology and human ingenuity to deliver better outcomes for all. ZSers drive impact by bringing a client-first mentality to each and every engagement. Bring your curiosity for learning, bold ideas, courage and passion to drive life-changing impact to ZS. 
 Insights & Analytics 
 ZS's Insights & Analytics group partners with clients to design and deliver solutions to help them tackle a broad range of business challenges. Our teams work on multiple projects simultaneously, leveraging advanced data analytics and problem-solving techniques. Our recommendations and solutions are based on rigorous research and analysis underpinned by deep expertise and thought leadership.    
 Decision Analytics Associate Consultant: Business Analytics & Insights 
 As a Decision Analytics Associate Consultant, you will serve as a strategic thought partner to client stakeholders, helping translate complex analytics into actionable business decisions. Working at the intersection of analytics, consulting and business strategy, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams to shape analytical approaches, guide problem-solving, interpret findings and communicate insights that drive impact. This role is ideal for professionals who enjoy connecting data to business outcomes, influencing decision-makers and partnering with teams to deliver meaningful results in a fast-growing and highly visible environment.

- Develop and apply analytical frameworks and statistical approaches that help clients understand complex business issues and make informed decisions. 
- Leverage analytic techniques to use data to guide clients and ZS team decision-making. 
- Partner with analytical teams to design and interpret analyses using tools such as SQL, Python, R, Excel, and cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks), and bring insights to life using Tableau, Power BI, or AI-assisted visualization tools. 
- Synthesize and communicate results to clients and ZS teams through oral and written presentations. 
- Develop client relationships and serve as key point of contact on aspects of projects. 
- Provide client and ZS teams project status updates. 
- Create project deliverables and implement solutions. 
- Advance problem-solving skills and improve ZS’s capabilities; 
- Guide and mentor Associates on teams. 
- Partner with clients and project teams to define business problems, shape analytical approaches and translate insights into strategic recommendations. 
- Guide and mentor analytical teams by providing direction, reviewing work quality and helping ensure solutions address key business objectives. 
- Serve as a trusted thought partner to stakeholders by connecting analytical findings to business implications and actionable outcomes. 
- Collaborate across cross-functional and global teams to drive alignment, solve complex business challenges and support decision-making. 
- Stay informed on emerging analytics and AI capabilities and identify opportunities to enhance business insights and client impact. What You’ll Bring

- Ability to connect analytical insights to business strategy and communicate findings effectively to diverse stakeholder groups. 
- Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams and influencing decision-making in a client-facing, consulting or business-partner capacity. 
- Demonstrated ability to guide workstreams, mentor junior team members and provide analytical direction. 
- Curiosity about emerging technologies and artificial intelligence, with an interest in applying new capabilities to business challenges.

WTW is seeking a highly analytical and technically skilled individual to join our Risk & Analytics team as a Physical Climate & Natural Catastrophe Risk Consultant. This role is ideal for candidates with a strong background in engineering, science, or analytics who are passionate about applying their expertise to real-world climate and catastrophe risk challenges.
 You will work alongside a multidisciplinary team of experts in insurance, science, and engineering to deliver cutting-edge risk assessments and consulting services to corporate clients across the U.S. and globally. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to innovative projects that span industries and geographies, with a focus on catastrophe risk engineering and climate resilience.
 The primary objectives are to support the Risk & Analytics team in advancing the catastrophe and climate risk management business in the US (primary focus) and globally. This includes providing assessments focused on catastrophe risk engineering, as well as leveraging RMS (Risk Management Solutions) models and other recognized catastrophe risk models in the insurance market, specifically for consulting projects delivered to WTW’s corporate clients. 
 We are open to hiring at a more junior level depending on the candidate’s experience.
 Note: visa employment-based non-immigrant visa sponsorship and/or assistance is not offered for this specific job opportunity.
 The Role 
- Conduct catastrophe risk engineering assessments and modeling analyses for corporate clients.
- Utilize and interpret outputs from catastrophe models (e.g., RMS, AIR, RQE, KatRisk).
- Support innovation in risk assessment where standard models or tools are unavailable.
- Evaluate property insurance portfolios and support climate-related financial disclosures across diverse asset types, including operational and construction-phase projects.
- Prepare technical reports and presentations to support insurance and risk decisions.
- Present findings to internal stakeholders and external clients.
- Perform data quality checks, hazard exposure analyses, and probabilistic modeling, ensuring results are robust and well-understood.
- Assist in business development, create proposals, and outline scope of work documents.
 -
 The Requirements 
- Strong academic background in engineering preferred (mechanical, civil, or structural preferred), science, mathematics, or a related field are also relevant.
- Solid understanding of catastrophe and probabilistic modeling principles.
- Experience with catastrophe risk engineering, including Probable Maximum Loss (PML) assessments and risk mitigation strategies.
- Proficiency with catastrophe modeling platforms such as RMS, AIR, RQE, or KatRisk.
- Familiarity with data analysis tools and languages such as SQL, R, and GIS.
- Experience in the insurance industry and understanding of policy structures is a plus.
- Ability to communicate complex technical and financial concepts to non-technical audiences.
- Strong leadership, presentation, and business development skills. 
 This position will remain posted for a minimum of three business days from the date posted or until sufficient/appropriate candidate slate has been identified.
 Compensation and Benefits 
 Base salary range and benefits information for this position are being included in accordance with requirements of various state/local pay transparency legislation.  Compensation

- Retirement Benefits: Qualified contributory pension plan (if eligible) and 401(k) plan with annual nonelective company contribution. Non-qualified retirement plans available to senior level colleagues who satisfy the plans’ eligibility requirements.

jd_text:
ERM is seeking a motivated EHS Consultant who is interested in paticipating a variety of projects covering the full spectrum of ERM’s services. 
 ERM delivers a wide range of services, including strategy development aligned with sustainability risks and opportunities, policy/regulatory analysis, peer benchmarking, operating model and organizational readiness, and action planning around core sustainability topics such as climate change/GHG emission reduction and circular economy.
 Responsibilities 
- Serve as the site EHS focal point, coordinating daily with the client, EPCC contractor, subcontractors and site teams. 
- Monitor compliance with applicable Malaysian EHS legislation, project approvals, permit conditions, contractual requirements and approved EHS plans and procedures. 
- Conduct routine inspections, joint walkthroughs and scheduled audits across construction areas, worker facilities, equipment, material storage and environmental controls. 
- Verify implementation of permit-to-work systems, risk assessments, job safety analyses, toolbox meetings, competency controls, emergency arrangements and incident-reporting procedures. 
- Review contractor submissions and records, including method statements, inspection reports, monitoring results, waste documentation, licences, permits, training records and statutory certificates. 
- Monitor controls for high-risk activities, including work at height, lifting, excavation, confined-space entry, electrical work, hot work, traffic management, mobile plant and simultaneous operations. 
- Monitor environmental controls for erosion and sediment, scheduled wastes, wastewater and effluent, dust, noise, air emissions, chemical storage, spills and sensitive receptors. 
- Record observations and non-conformances, agree corrective actions with the EPCC contractor, and verify close-out within the required timeframe. 
- Support incident notification, investigation and root-cause analysis, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure. 
- Participate in site coordination and EHS meetings, progress reviews and emergency drills; promptly escalate significant, repeated or overdue issues to client site management. 
- Prepare clear daily, weekly and monthly reports covering compliance status, inspection findings, incidents, performance indicators, outstanding actions and emerging risks. 
- Liaise with regulatory authorities when authorised by the client and support inspections, submissions and follow-up actions. 
- Exercise stop-work authority in accordance with project procedures where there is imminent danger, serious non-compliance or unacceptable environmental risk. 
- Maintain complete, current and auditable site EHS records. 
 Requirements 
- Degree or diploma in environmental science, engineering, occupational safety and health, construction management or a related technical discipline. 
- Minimum 5 years of site-based EHS experience on construction, infrastructure, industrial or energy projects, including direct coordination with an EPCC or main contractor and subcontractors. 
- Proven experience in site inspections, compliance audits, contractor-document reviews, incident investigations and corrective-action close-out. 
- Strong working knowledge of Malaysian environmental and occupational safety and health legislation, licences, permits, approval conditions and construction-site compliance requirements. 
- Valid Malaysian competency certification or registration relevant to the project scope, such as Safety and Health Officer, Site Safety Supervisor, a Department of Environment competent-person certification, or another recognised DOSH or DOE credential. 
- Applicants must provide the certification title, issuing authority, registration or certificate number, competency scope and validity period before mobilisation. 
- Practical knowledge of construction controls, including permit-to-work, risk assessment, lifting, excavation, work at height, confined spaces, hot work, traffic management and emergency response. 
- Practical awareness of electrical safety, including temporary installations and distribution boards, isolation and lockout/tagout, energised-work interfaces, earthing, residual-current protection, cable management, portable tools and coordination with authorised electrical personnel. 
- Practical knowledge of construction environmental controls, including scheduled wastes, wastewater, erosion and sediment, dust, noise, chemical storage and spill response. 
- Ability to identify non-compliance, reference the applicable requirement and communicate practical actions to the EPCC conConfident communicator able to engage site management, supervisors, workers, contractors and regulators in English and Bahasa Malaysia. 
- Ability to prepare concise site reports, meeting records and escalation notes. 
- Willing and physically able to work predominantly at site, undertake frequent inspections, wear required personal protective equipment and operate safely within active construction areas. 
- Valid driving licence and ability to travel to and within the project site. 
- Applicants must submit a project credential sheet stating each relevant assignment’s project type, location, duration, role, EPCC or contractor interface, key responsibilities and associated competency certifications.

 You will help deliver high-quality work that drives impactful programs for our clients, while building strong relationships and contributing fresh ideas to evolve our services. jd_text:
Description 
 About Alvarez & Marsal 
 Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M. 
 The Team 
 The Healthcare Industry Group, a subsidiary of A&M, leads transformational change in healthcare. As established leaders and trusted advisors, we deliver results for healthcare executives, boards, private equity firms, investors, law firms, and government agencies. Our team brings diverse perspectives and experiences to assist clients with enhancing financial and operational performance, accelerating strategic growth, and optimizing value throughout the investment lifecycle.
 A practice within the Healthcare Industry Group (HIG), the Human Capital and Workforce Management (HCWM) service line is comprised of knowledgeable workforce management and human resources professionals experienced in the healthcare space. This team leads transformational work to meet client goals in a rapidly evolving and dynamic labor market that includes post-transaction integration, organizational design, alignment of staffing to business strategy and demand, change management, workforce cost takeout, and development of talent acquisition, employee engagement and management strategies.
 As part of the HCWM team, you will have the opportunity to work with clients in a variety of sectors including: health systems and providers, physician groups, ancillary providers, medical schools, vision, laboratory, dental and behavioral health, managed care and health plans, government plans and programs, healthcare investors and lenders, medical devices, healthcare suppliers and infrastructure, life sciences, pharma, and biotech.
 How you will contribute 
 As a Consultant, you will be working closely with healthcare clients on a range of complex assignments. You will work in a team environment while using your independent judgment and critical thinking skills to provide practical solutions and add value for our clients.
 Revenue cycle projects may include, but are not limited to due diligences, performance assessments, enterprise performance improvement, full-scale implementations, and interim management for a broad range of healthcare providers and supporting services companies. Depending on the client project the responsibilities of a consultant may typically include:
- Building and maintaining financial and operational models to assess client performance and inform recommendations 
- Benchmarking and root cause analyses, including data sampling to identify performance gaps and improvement opportunities 
- Mapping out processes and performing gap analyses while managing both client and internal projects. 
- Conducting client interviews and observations to define current state and identifying actionable items for improvement. 
- Analyzing and sampling data for root cause analysis. 
- Preparing and communicating client-ready deliverables. Assisting with the development of presentations, pitch and proposal content. 
- Managing assigned workstreams or projects, coordinating inputs and driving work to completion Our consultants possess a high aptitude for financial and operational analysis and will leverage their excellent written and verbal communication skills to work with senior leaders and clients. We are seeking someone to join our team with an entrepreneurial and collaborative mindset who works well with ambiguity and thrives in a fast-paced environment. As a Consultant you will have the opportunity to demonstrate your leadership, integrity and objectivity when interacting with clients at all corporate levels.
 We are not your typical consulting firm. We are entrepreneurial, action oriented and results driven professionals who take a hands-on approach to solving our clients’ problems and helping them drive value and growth. We are nimble, resourceful, proactive, can pivot to adapt quickly, when needed, and develop plans that drive real results. You will be part of a team that is passionate about delivering transformational change and making an impact in the healthcare industry.
 Qualifications include: 
- A minimum of three (3) years of prior work experience in healthcare, consulting or healthcare industry such as revenue cycle, hospital, accounting, audit, private equity, or healthcare operations with a healthcare focus. 
- BA/BS degree and/or MBA/MS in Accounting, Finance, or other related healthcare fields such as MHA or MPH. 
- Foundational understanding of the healthcare industry, including workforce strategy, operations, or labor market trends 
- Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills with an ability to translate data into insights 
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to create clear and professional client deliverables 
- Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, and Word; familiarity with tools such as Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Action O-I benchmarking, or MGMA survey data a plus 
- Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within cross-functional teams 
- Eagerness to learn, take initiative, and contribute to a growing, entrepreneurial practice 
- Willingness and ability to travel as required Your journey at A&M 
 We recognize that our people are the driving force behind our success, which is why we prioritize an employee experience that fosters each person’s unique professional and personal development. Our robust performance development process promotes continuous learning, rewards your contributions, and fosters a culture of meritocracy. With top-notch training and on-the-job learning opportunities, you can acquire new skills and advance your career.
 We prioritize your well-being, providing benefits and resources to support you on your personal journey. Our people consistently highlight the growth opportunities, our unique, entrepreneurial culture, and the fun we have together as their favorite aspects of working at A&M. The possibilities are endless for high-performing and passionate professionals.
 Regular employees working 30 or more hours per week are also entitled to participate in Alvarez & Marsal Holdings’ fringe benefits consisting of healthcare plans, flexible spending and savings accounts, life, AD&D, and disability coverages at rates determined periodically as well as a 401(k) retirement savings plan. Provided the eligibility requirements are met, employees will also receive an annual discretionary contribution to their 401(k) retirement savings plan from Alvarez & Marsal. Additionally, employees are eligible for paid time off including vacation, personal days, seventy-two (72) hours of sick time (prorated for part time employees), ten federal holidays, one floating holiday, and parental leave. The amount of vacation and personal days available varies based on tenure and role type. Click here for more information regarding A&M’s benefits programs.
 The salary range is $100,000- $120,000 annually, dependent on several variables including but not limited to education, experience, skills, and geography. In addition, A&M offers a discretionary bonus program which is based on a number of factors, including individual and firm performance. Please ask your recruiter for details.

Role Summary In Accenture Operations, we are looking for a highly motivated Business Transformation Analyst to support clients in designing, implementing, scaling, and optimizing enterprise transformation initiatives across industries. Part of the role will focus on helping clients design, set up, scale, and improve Global Capability Centers (GCCs). At the same time, the role remains broader, meaning that you will work on a broad range of topics related to business transformations. This covers operating model transformation, governance frameworks, service delivery improvements, talent strategies, technology enablement, and transformation roadmaps for our clients, where you will typically work as a business analyst, support in these changes. The ideal candidate combines strong analytical skills, structured problem-solving, stakeholder engagement, and execution discipline, with an interest in how GCCs, Shared Services, Global Business Services, AI, automation, and analytics can help organizations build scalable capabilities and deliver measurable business outcomes. Accenture Operations As part of Accenture Operations, you focus on executing plans efficiently and achieving short-term objectives in line with the strategic goals. Within Operations, we also typically have longer engagements to ensure effective transformations, and the right capacity and capabilities are in place. You will work together with our colleagues from different reinvention partners such as Talent, Digital Core and Industry & Enterprise. While their focus will be on setting up the operating model, our focus on Operations is to work together on implementing and executing the change and ensuring a smooth transformation for clients by achieving operational excellence. You typically work with mid-level management and department heads at the client and make a bridge to their operations through a hands-on approach. Key Responsibilities Transformation Delivery Support the planning and execution of business transformation, enterprise operating model, service delivery improvement, and capability-building initiatives across industries. Support clients in defining and executing GCC-related transformation initiatives, including setup, scale-up, optimization, transition planning, and value realization. Contribute to operating model design activities, including service scope, governance, talent considerations, process ownership, location considerations, and technology enablement. Help shape GCC operating models by supporting capability maps, service portfolios, governance forums, KPIs, SLAs, escalation paths, and decision-making structures. Support maturity assessments, benchmarking studies, business case development, transition planning, and value realization. Support transformation planning across business functions, retained organizations, operational teams, and third-party partners. Develop an understanding of how AI, automation, analytics, process excellence, and digital tools can improve productivity, operational performance, scalability, and business outcomes. Assist in developing transformation roadmaps, implementation plans, milestones, RAID logs, delivery trackers, and value realization updates. Support process documentation, process mapping, and process improvement activities. Analysis & Insights Analyze operating models, organizational structures, service delivery models, governance frameworks, capability structures, and business processes. Develop insights and recommendations supported by qualitative and quantitative analysis. Create reports and presentation materials for client and internal discussions. Stakeholder Management Collaborate with client stakeholders, internal teams, and subject matter experts across business, operations, technology, HR, finance, and transformation functions. Support workshops, meetings, and working sessions to gather requirements and structure discussions Change Management & PMO Support change management and adoption activities linked to new processes, tools, roles, service delivery models, and ways of working. Track progress against milestones, KPIs, value realization metrics, transition deliverables, and agreed transformation outcomes. Support project management activities including planning, reporting, dependency management, issue resolution, resource coordination, and status updates.
Qualifications Required Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Finance, Operations, or a related discipline. 1-2 years of experience in consulting, enterprise transformation, PMO, operations, change management, or business transformation. Fluency in Dutch and excellent command of English. Strong analytical, structured problem-solving, and data storytelling skills. Excellent PowerPoint, Excel, and executive communication capabilities. Familiarity with Agile methodologies, project management, change management, PMO practices, and transformation delivery disciplines. Experience with Power BI or Tableau. Awareness of AI-enabled transformation, automation, analytics, digital productivity tools, or process excellence initiatives. Interest in Global Capability Centers (GCCs), Shared Services, Global Business Services (GBS), service delivery models, or enterprise operating model transformation. Exposure to process mapping, process documentation, and continuous improvement methodologies. Exposure to change management and adoption activities. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced consulting environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Preferred Experience supporting or contributing to GCC, Shared Services, GBS, service delivery, operating model, or enterprise transformation initiatives. Understanding of GCC concepts, service transition, governance models, value realization, talent strategies, location strategy, and continuous improvement. Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt certification, training, or practical exposure; Green Belt exposure is a plus. Key Competencies Structured problem solving Analytical thinking Communication & storytelling Collaboration & teamwork Adaptability & learning agility Results orientation

- Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Associates and Associate Consultants — setting the standard for research quality, client presence, and professional growth

- Gain immediate familiarity with client’s internal processes.

- Fluency in English

jd_text:
Joining Arup 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.
 Watch this short clip to discover how Arup are shaping a better world and how you could be a part of it! 
 The Opportunity 
 We are looking for talented People and Change consultants who are looking to grow their career in the infrastructure sector. Based in London you will join a growing Advisory practice which is specialising in helping drive change and transformation across organisations operating across the built environment, predominantly in Manufacturing, Rail, Highways, Energy, Aviation and Water.
 You will be responsible for technical delivery on one or more management consultant projects with oversight and support from Arup Project Manager/Director. Our commitment to technical quality is matched by our commitment to building high quality and enduring relationships with our clients. You will be responsible for managing the day-to-day deliverables, listening and understanding our client needs and responding appropriately and pro-actively to feedback.
 These exciting opportunities will suit consultants who are keen to take the next step in their career. You will have the opportunity to work with a diverse group of clients and fellow Arup colleagues from multiple technical disciplines. 
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective – in which we encourage individuality to thrive. Our strength comes from how we respect, share and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives and ideas. You will have the opportunity do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, to our members and to the clients and communities we serve.
 Is this role right for you? 
 We are seeking consultants with a background in a consulting or in-house environment with experience in two or more of our technical areas (team effectiveness & collaboration, leadership & capability, culture & organisational change, operating model & organisation development). You will have the following skills and experience:
- Typically, a degree and/or extensive experience in business or related discipline (HR, change management, management consulting or occupational psychology) and chartered or working towards becoming a chartered management consultant.
- A background in the built environment, predominantly in Water, Energy, Rail, Highways, Aviation and Manufacturing.
- Project management and delivery skills including financial and risk management.
- Experience using recognised research and data analysis tools (e.g. surveys, interviews, workforce and organisational data analysis).
- Capability in developing business proposals for clients by understanding their requirements and drawing together expertise from a multi-disciplinary firm.
 Unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK at the time of application and for the duration of employment. Any offer made will be subject to satisfactory proof of immigration status.
 Not ready to apply just yet or have some questions? Contact Anna Lipka at anna.lipka@arup.com - Please note, to ensure we remain GDPR compliant do not send your CV directly to us via this email.
 What We Offer you 
 At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
 Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
 We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
 We also provide Private medical insurance, Life assurance, Accident insurance and Income protection cover. In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.
 Different People, Shared Values 
 Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas – this drives our excellence.
 Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup. 
 We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible to all candidates. Please contact Rachel Connolly at rachel.connolly@arup.com to let us know if you need any assistance or reasonable adjustments throughout your application or interview process, and/or to perform the essential functions of the role. We will do everything we can to support you.
 Our Application Process 
 To understand what to expect next, please visit https://www.arup.com/careers/recruitment-process/ 
 Stay safe online – Arup will never ask for your bank details as part of our recruitment process.
 Recruitment Agencies 
 We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on the list.
 Closing date: 19 th of November
 We may close the role earlier than the advertised date should we receive a large number of applications, so please ensure you apply early.

In addition to delivering more advanced energy modelling, this core team is responsible for training and skills development for engineers working in these areas.
 The successful candidate for this role will be responsible for delivery of advanced energy modelling across a number of projects, including both undertaking modelling directly and guiding graduates and apprentices in the development of IES models. We are able to support the successful candidate through their Chartership journey.
 The role will include: 
 · Undertaking advanced energy modelling including for TM54, NABERS and bespoke project requirements, using a combination of IES-VE, including APACHE HVAC, spreadsheets and other advanced analytics tools as needed.

 · Contribute to the development of training resources and the delivery of advanced energy modelling training for our engineers. 
 · Contribute to the delivery of research focused on improving the tools, techniques and approaches we employ for advanced energy modelling. 
 · The role will be based in Central London but may involve some travel l ing nationally and internationally.

 · Experience in Data Analysis using Excel.
 · Developing understanding of building HVAC systems and controls.
 · Degree in an area such as; mechanical engineering, building services, architectural engineering, building physics.

jd_text:
Shape a future with purpose at Arup in Milan. 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world. 
 Dedicated to sustainable development, Arup is a collective of advisors and experts working across 140 countries. Founded to be both humane and excellent, we collaborate with our clients and partners using imagination, technology and rigour to shape a better world. 
 Our award-winning global transaction advisory team is growing, and we are looking for a consultant to deliver technical advisory assignments to support clients investing in renewables and storage assets and companies. 
 The Opportunity 
 We are looking for people with project development, operation, engineering, commercial or transaction experience on a range of technologies, including solar, wind, BESS and energy transition. 
 The focus of due diligence work is to help evaluate potential investments by identifying and assessing technical, operational, commercial and reputational risks and opportunities. 
 As a Consultant at Arup, you will: 
- Work on discrete projects, typically consisting of technical, ESG or commercial due diligence, to inform buyers or sellers of assets and companies in the energy transition space. 
- Conduct wider advisory work to support clients navigating the energy transition, in accordance with the individual’s skillsets. 
 Other activities may include: 
- Contributing to project management tasks 
- Taking part to research and analysis assignments. 
- Contributing to bid development for due diligence assignments. 
- Taking part to conversations with clients. 
- Contributing to sectoral knowledge through data analysis. 
- Process improvement and continuous development. 
 Does this role inspire you? 
- We're looking for someone who is passionate about renewable energy advisory services. We also value: 
- Relevant engineering or environmental related degree, or equivalent experience with renewable energy technologies. 
- At least 1-2 years of professional experience in solar, wind, BESS or hybrid systems . 
- Experience in other European markets beside Italy will be appreciated. 
- Any prior experience of undertaking technical due diligence services on energy infrastructure assets. 
- Fluency in both written and spoken English, you have quantitative and analytical skills, and good knowledge of both Excel and PowerPoint. 
 Why Arup? 
 At Arup, we believe in rewarding our members for their contributions to our shared success. As a trust-owned company, we have the freedom to pursue meaningful work that aligns with our purpose and values. We also offer a unique profit share program, allowing our members to share in the results of our collective efforts. 
 Benefits that work for you: 
- Professional Growth & Development: Benefit from continuous learning opportunities, training programs, and mentorship to enhance your skills and advance your career at Arup. 
- Global Opportunities: Collaborate with colleagues worldwide and explore potential short-term or long-term assignments at other Arup offices and project locations. 
- Financial Well-being & Ownership: Receive a competitive salary and benefits package and share in Arup's success through our global profit-sharing programme. 
- Flexible Working: Possibility to work from home for part of the week. 
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective where individuality is encouraged. Our strength comes from how we respect, share, and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas. You'll have the opportunity to do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, and to the clients and communities we serve. 
 We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of the world around us. We actively promote a culture of inclusion where everyone feels welcome, respected, and valued. 
 We welcome applications from talented individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, disability, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible. If you need any assistance or adjustments, please visit our Candidate Support page for contact information and assistance. We're happy to help. 
 Do you want to join us in shaping a better world? 
 The gross annual salary (RAL) for this role is €29,500 to €34,000, in accordance with the applicable provisions of the CCNL Terziario (Confcommercio). The final salary is determined using objective and gender-neutral criteria, reflecting experience, qualifications and role-relevant skills.

jd_text:
Shape a future with purpose at Arup in Milan. 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 75 years, guiding how we shape a better world. 
 Our award-winning Business and Investor Advisory (BIA) team is a market leader in infrastructure and energy advisory services. We're looking for infrastructure and energy engineering graduates passionate about strategy and investments.
 We work across international markets, providing strategic, and technical advice throughout the project lifecycle. With expertise spanning energy, transport, social infrastructure, and utilities, our work supports investors, asset owners, operators, governments, and financial institutions.
 The Opportunity 
 You will be working on individual projects, typically comprising technical and environmental, social and governance (ESG) due diligence to inform lenders, buyers or sellers of infrastructure and energy projects. The focus of the technical due diligence work is to assist in the evaluation of potential investments by identifying and assessing technical, operational, commercial and reputational risks and opportunities.
 The successful candidate will be responsible for providing a range of quantitative skills, from data handling and presentation to financial/economic modelling.
 We are looking for team members who will support the organic growth of the group and the expansion of our activities in the coming years. This provides opportunities for professional growth and rewards individual proactivity.
 The role will also extend to carrying out wider advisory work in the public and private sectors, as appropriate to the individual's skills.
 As an Infrastructure Investment Consultant at Arup, you will: 
- Assist with project management tasks, with increasing responsibility over time.
- Conduct research and analysis, contributing directly to key project insights.
- Build deep sector expertise through hands-on experience and structured learning.
- Support client-facing tasks, working towards client interaction.
- Work on process improvement and development.
- Collaborate with teams both in Italy and internationally, working closely with technical experts and collaborating with colleagues based in other offices across global projects.
 Does this role inspire you? 
 We're looking for graduates who are passionate about energy , transport , industry and technology markets . We also value:
- A relevant engineering degree, or equivalent experience with infrastructure projects including transport (highways, rails, metro, airports, smart and low emission mobility), social infrastructures (hospitals, schools), utilities and data centres.
- 0 to 3 years of post-graduation experience and track record in commercial or transaction due diligences in the infrastructure sector.
- Strong quantitative and analytical skills.
- Strong knowledge of both Excel and PowerPoint.
- You are fluent in Italian and both written and spoken English.
- Team player, good under delivery pressure whilst maintain quality outputs.
- Ability to rapidly switch from infrastructure-related projects in different fields.
 Why Arup? 
 At Arup, we believe in investing in our people and supporting their growth from day one. As a trust-owned company, we're driven by our purpose and values, creating a collaborative and rewarding environment for our employees.
 Benefits that work for you: 
- Professional Growth & Development: Kickstart your career with our structured graduate development program, benefit from continuous learning opportunities, and receive guidance from experienced mentors. 
- Global Opportunities: Collaborate with colleagues worldwide and explore potential short-term or long-term assignments at other Arup offices and project locations. 
- Financial Well-being & Ownership: Receive a competitive graduate salary and benefits package and share in Arup's success through our global profit-sharing program. In Italy, the gross annual salary (RAL) for this role is €29,500 to €34,000, in accordance with the applicable provisions of the CCNL Terziario (Confcommercio). The final salary is determined using objective and gender-neutral criteria, reflecting experience, qualifications and role-relevant skills. 
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective where individuality is encouraged. Our strength comes from how we respect, share, and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas. You'll have the opportunity to do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, and to the clients and communities we serve.
 We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of the world around us. We actively promote a culture of inclusion where everyone feels welcome, respected, and valued.
 We welcome applications from talented individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, disability, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible. If you need any assistance or adjustments, please visit our Candidate Support page for contact information and assistance. We're happy to help.
 Do you want to join us in shaping a better world?

jd_text:
Joining Arup 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.
 Watch this short clip to discover how Arup are shaping a better world and how you could be a part of it! 
 The Opportunity 
 Our North Advisory People & Organisations team are expanding and seeking a People & Organisations Consultant in Edinburgh or Glasgow, where you will apply knowledge of organisational transformation, people and change to deliver complex client engagements, improving the performance of organisations, assets and people through practical, implementable solutions.
 You will be responsible for delivering larger and/or more complex components of projects, applying knowledge of a defined capability area (e.g. organisational development, culture & change, leadership, team effectiveness) and applying structured, evidence-based analysis to diagnose organisational challenges and derive actionable insights. You will then translate your analysis into practical recommendations that improve organisational performance and enable change.
 Other aspects of the role include:
- Designing and delivering organisational diagnostics, workshops and outputs grounded in recognised theory and practice.
- Building and managing effective client and internal relationships to support delivery and collaboration. Contributing to proposal development, work winning and network building.
- Delivering work in line with agreed scope, quality and commercial expectations and contributing to the development of methodologies, tools and capability within the People & Organisation practice.
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective – in which we encourage individuality to thrive. Our strength comes from how we respect, share and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives and ideas. You will have the opportunity do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, to our members and to the clients and communities we serve. 
 Is this role right for you? 
 We are seeking individuals to support delivery of business transformation outcomes through integration of people, organisation and operational considerations. You will have knowledge across two or more of:
- Operating model & organisational development.
- Culture transformation & organisational change.
- Team effectiveness & collaboration.
- Leadership & capability.
 The following qualifications and experiences are required:
- Degree in relevant discipline and working towards relevant professional accreditation (e.g. CIPD, BPS).
- A track record in consulting or relevant in-house roles with experience in at least two People & Organisation capability areas.
- Analytical capability, including use of recognised research and data analysis approaches.
 Not ready to apply just yet or have some questions? Contact Rachel Connolly at rachel.connolly@arup.com Please note – to ensure we remain GDPR compliant, do not send your CV directly to this email.
 ***Unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK at the time of application and for the duration of employment. Any offer made will be subject to satisfactory proof of immigration status***
 What We Offer you 
 At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
 Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
 We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
 We also provide Private medical insurance, Life assurance, Accident insurance and Income protection cover. In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits   to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.
 Different People, Shared Values 
 Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas – this drives our excellence.
 Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup. 
 We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible to all candidates. Please contact Rachel Connolly at rachel.connolly@arup.com to let us know if you need any assistance or reasonable adjustments throughout your application or interview process, and/or to perform the essential functions of the role. We will do everything we can to support you.
 Our Application Process 
 To understand what to expect next, please visit https://www.arup.com/careers/recruitment-process/ 
 Stay safe online – Arup will never ask for your bank details as part of our recruitment process.
 Recruitment Agencies 
 We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on the list.

jd_text:
Joining Arup 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach have set us apart for 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world. 
 Our Economics and Casemaking practice sits within the Cities, Planning and Design (CPD) team and is at the forefront of thinking about the future of places. We work with clients to understand the economic, social and spatial value of places, helping them articulate compelling stories, build robust cases for investment, and deliver inclusive and sustainable growth.
 Watch this short clip to discover how Arup are shaping a better world and how you could be a part of it!
 The Opportunity 
 We are looking for a Consultant to join our Economics & Casemaking team in Leeds, part of a national practice working at the forefront of shaping cities and places.
 You’ll support a wide range of projects across regeneration, economic development, infrastructure and growth, helping clients build compelling cases for investment, develop strategies for inclusive and sustainable growth, and deliver complex programmes. This includes contributing to business cases, strategy and vision documents, socio‑economic analysis, impact assessments and social value work.
 Working as part of collaborative, multidisciplinary project teams, you’ll engage with public sector clients, developers and other stakeholders, providing clear, evidence‑based advice in dynamic and often long‑term environments. You’ll work closely with colleagues across Arup, including planners, designers, transport and sustainability specialists.
 You don’t need experience in every area. We’re an inclusive team and welcome applicants with a strong interest in cities, regions and the built environment, who are keen to learn, grow and make a positive impact from day one.
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective – in which we encourage individuality to thrive. Our strength comes from how we respect, share and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives and ideas.
You will have the opportunity to do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, to our members and to the clients and communities we serve.
 Is this role right for you? 
 We’re looking for someone who is curious, motivated and enjoys working collaboratively. You’ll bring:
- A degree (or working towards one) in economics, geography, regeneration, real estate, public or social policy, business, town planning or a related built‑environment discipline 
- Strong written communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to produce clear, engaging reports and presentations 
- Confidence communicating verbally, including contributing to meetings, workshops and presentations 
- Analytical and research skills, with the ability to interpret data and synthesise information 
- A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for working as part of a team 
- Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage time and priorities effectively 
- A genuine interest in the built environment, including urban regeneration, housing, transport, net zero and related current affairs Experience with tools such as GIS, PowerBI, economic modelling or Better Business Case training is welcomed but not essential.
 This role does not meet the criteria for visa sponsorship under the UK immigration system. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. 
 Not ready to apply just yet or have some questions? Contact Drina Zupanovic at Drina.Zupanovicgerard@arup.com - Please note, to ensure we remain GDPR compliant do not send your CV directly to us via this email.
 What we offer you 
 At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
 Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
 We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
 We also provide Private medical insurance, Life assurance, Accident insurance and Income protection cover. In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.
 Different people, shared values 
 Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas – this drives our excellence.
 Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup. 
 We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible to all candidates. Please contact Drina.Zupanovicgerard@arup.com to let us know if you need any assistance or reasonable adjustments throughout your application or interview process, and/or to perform the essential functions of the role. We will do everything we can to support you.
 Our Application Process 
 To understand what to expect next, please visit https://www.arup.com/careers/recruitment-process/ 
 Stay safe online – Arup will never ask for your bank details as part of our recruitment process.
 Recruitment Agencies – We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on the list.
 Closing Date: 29.10.2026
 We may close the role earlier than the advertised date should we receive a large number of applications, so please ensure you apply early.

jd_text:
Position: Associate Consultant - Corporate Advisory
Location: Bengaluru

We Partner to deliver social impact at scale

Sattva Consulting is a global impact consulting firm from India. Since 2009 we have been engaging with communities, business and government to achieve societal impact at scale.

We believe that Civil society, Business and Government all have a critical role to play in building an equitable and sustainable world, and we actively partner with all stakeholders to enable impact through our advisory & orchestration services, knowledge and data platforms which we have built as public goods for the ecosystem and collaborative solutions and partnerships.

Our teams are based in India, Singapore, Denmark and UK, but as a global organization our work has spanned 25 countries and 5 continents. For more information, please visit: www.sattva.co.in 

The Opportunity

The Associate Consultant will play a key role in designing solutions to meet CSR customer needs and drive measurable social impact. You'll collaborate with the corporate sector in India, contributing to business development efforts and working across various thematic areas.
The candidate will be based out of the client's office for five days/week.

In addition, the following will be the key responsibilities:
Ensure effective and frequent communication with internal and external stakeholders through sharing detailed work plans, project governance decks, and minutes

Lead primary and secondary research to arrive at insights required to solve problems

Contribute to problem-solving and ideating for solutions through different frameworks, creating and validating hypotheses

Program monitoring of mid-to-large sized programs within CSR portfolio

Document and prepare key project artifacts notes/decks/databases/excels to ensure efficient delivery of quality client-facing products

Create reports and tools to inform the effectiveness of the project.

Document learnings to create reusable knowledge from the project

Contribute to the creation of proposals after understanding project financials at a headline level

Go beyond own deliverables to support others in the team or the larger organization where required

Support in the documentation of learnings and potentially the creation of reusable knowledge from the project

The Ideal Candidate

At Sattva, our goal is to realize the impact on the ground and to drive a collective win by engaging with multiple stakeholders. We are looking for individuals who align with our mission of alleviating poverty in our lifetime and have the following profile:

A minimum of 2-4 years of project and stakeholder management experience (preferable if in the social sector)

Proficiency in Kannada (Read , Write and Speak)

An understanding of the roles of various stakeholders in the development landscape (corporate organizations, government, and non-profit)

Knowledge of communications and reporting is preferable

Working knowledge of Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) frameworks

Ability to work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment as part of a closely- knit team

Outstanding verbal and written communication skills with exceptional attention to
detail

Highly effective interpersonal skills

Self-driven personality with the ability to work independently

Why Sattva?

It's not about us really- Because IMPACT is everybody’s business.
Create Impact: Make an impact with the work you do and solutions you design

Work Environment: Thrive in a diverse, inclusive and collaborative environment

Learn & Grow: Challenge yourself to learn, grow and deliver the best you can

Future Ready: Work on critical issues of today that will affect our collective tomorrow

Sattva is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants regardless of race, religion, caste, creed, gender, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, or any other legally protected and/or marginalized characteristics. Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are essential to our business and we foster an environment of respect and a culture that celebrates diversity and promotes equity and inclusion. We are committed to providing all employees with education, training, and development opportunities to create a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and included.
